counterfactual.change: changed single field bodies[0].e from 0.90698 to 0.0 (inelastic). All else identical including 61 steps. With e=0 bounce dissipates energy, same trajectory no longer exceeds energy bound, proving violation is caused by restitution-dependent collision energy injection.

explanation: Single body bounce violates energy conservation: high restitution (e=0.907) floor collision injects energy instead of dissipating it. Pre-impact speed ~18.67 m/s at step 60 should rebound at ~e*vin ≈16.9 m/s, but post-impact speed at step 61 is 19.73 m/s, larger than inbound, raising total mechanical energy from ~3017 J to 3363 J (limit 3324 J) with zero controller work. Likely impulse/positional-correction bug that adds energy on high-velocity substepped collision (7 substeps in step 61).
vision_note: A single blue circular body falls vertically toward the floor across frames 58-60 and is in contact with the bottom boundary in frame 61. No extra bodies, walls, waypoints or penetration/tunneling is visible; the motion appears as a normal gravity-driven drop to impact with no obvious large rebound in the still frames.
